install.agentPrompt:
The user typed this into the Skills install box:

---
{{input}}
---

Please help them install it patiently: work out which skill they mean (fetch the URL, search for it, or ask them if it is ambiguous), then save it as a skill file at .dsh/skills/<name>/SKILL.md inside this workspace - never outside it; the app then makes it available in every workspace. The dsh-skill-module documents the format. Finally reply with the installed skill's name.

environment.detectionUnavailable: Environment detection runs in the desktop app.
environment.connectToInstall: Connect the runtime to request an installation.
environment.note: DeepSeek Harness runs code with whatever is installed here (e.g. Python via its shell tool). uv ships with the app, and Jupyter can be app-managed in Settings -> Connectors. On Windows, MatterGen commonly runs in a WSL2/Linux GPU environment; a missing native venv does not mean PyTorch or MatterGen is missing from WSL2. Missing components can be installed through a governed model task after it checks your local OS, GPU, driver, and Python compatibility. MatterGen source ships with the app; the default chemical_system checkpoint is installed separately from this page and verified before use.
